units.leftText: This is the burden against Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:
units.rightText: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.

units.leftText: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on His foes and reserves wrath for His enemies.
units.rightText: Jehovah is a jealous God and avengeth; Jehovah avengeth and is full of wrath; Jehovah taketh vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies.

units.leftText: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.
units.rightText: Jehovah is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means clear the guilty: Jehovah hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.

units.leftText: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.
units.rightText: He rebuketh the sea, and maketh it dry, and drieth up all the rivers: Bashan languisheth, and Carmel; and the flower of Lebanon languisheth.

units.leftText: The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth trembles at His presence— the world and all its dwellers.
units.rightText: The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt; and the earth is upheaved at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein.

units.leftText: Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; even rocks are shattered before Him.
units.rightText: Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken asunder by him.

units.leftText: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; He cares for those who trust in Him.
units.rightText: Jehovah is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that take refuge in him.

units.leftText: But with an overwhelming flood He will make an end of Nineveh and pursue His enemies into darkness.
units.rightText: But with an over-running flood he will make a full end of her place, and will pursue his enemies into darkness.

units.leftText: Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end. Affliction will not rise up a second time.
units.rightText: What do ye devise against Jehovah? he will make a full end; affliction shall not rise up the second time.

units.leftText: For they will be entangled as with thorns and consumed like the drink of a drunkard — like stubble that is fully dry.
units.rightText: For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly as dry stubble.

units.leftText: From you, O Nineveh, comes forth a plotter of evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.
units.rightText: There is one gone forth out of thee, that deviseth evil against Jehovah, that counselleth wickedness.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “Though they are allied and numerous, yet they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, O Judah, I will afflict you no longer.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: Though they be in full strength, and likewise many, even so shall they be cut down, and he shall pass away. Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more.

units.leftText: For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.”
units.rightText: And now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.

units.leftText: The LORD has issued a command concerning you, O Nineveh: “There will be no descendants to carry on your name. I will cut off the carved image and cast idol from the house of your gods; I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah hath given commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image; I will make thy grave; for thou art vile.

units.leftText: Look to the mountains— the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the wicked will never again march through you; they will be utterly cut off.
units.rightText: Behold, upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace! Keep thy feasts, O Judah, perform thy vows; for the wicked one shall no more pass through thee; he is utterly cut off.

units.leftText: One who scatters advances against you, O Nineveh. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourselves! Summon all your strength!
units.rightText: He that dasheth in pieces is come up against thee: keep the fortress, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily.

units.leftText: For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined the branches of their vine.
units.rightText: For Jehovah restoreth the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel; for the emptiers have emptied them out, and destroyed their vine-branches.

units.leftText: The shields of his mighty men are red; the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet. The fittings of the chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the spears of cypress have been brandished.
units.rightText: The shield of his mighty men is made red, the valiant men are in scarlet: the chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the cypress spears are brandished.
leftNotes: 2:3 Hebrew; alternately, the spears may be of pine or juniper or fir; LXX and Syriac they are prepared, and the horsemen rush to and fro.

units.leftText: The chariots dash through the streets; they rush around the plazas, appearing like torches, darting about like lightning.
units.rightText: The chariots rage in the streets; they rush to and fro in the broad ways: the appearance of them is like torches; they run like the lightnings.

units.leftText: He summons his nobles; they stumble as they advance. They race to its wall; the protective shield is set in place.
units.rightText: He remembereth his nobles: they stumble in their march; they make haste to the wall thereof, and the mantelet is prepared.

units.leftText: The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses.
units.rightText: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.

units.leftText: It is decreed that the city be exiled and carried away; her maidservants moan like doves, and beat upon their breasts.
units.rightText: And it is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her handmaids moan as with the voice of doves, beating upon their breasts.

units.leftText: Nineveh has been like a pool of water throughout her days, but now it is draining away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one turns back.
units.rightText: But Nineveh hath been from of old like a pool of water: yet they flee away. Stand, stand, they cry; but none looketh back.

units.leftText: “Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold!” There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
units.rightText: Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold; for there is no end of the store, the glory of all goodly furniture.

units.leftText: She is emptied! Yes , she is desolate and laid waste! Hearts melt, knees knock, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale!
units.rightText: She is empty, and void, and waste; and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and anguish is in all loins, and the faces of them all are waxed pale.

units.leftText: Where is the lions’ lair or the feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion and lioness prowled with their cubs, with nothing to frighten them away?
units.rightText: Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding-place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked, the lion’s whelp, and none made them afraid?

units.leftText: The lion mauled enough for its cubs and strangled prey for the lioness. It filled its dens with the kill, and its lairs with mauled prey.
units.rightText: The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his caves with prey, and his dens with ravin.

units.leftText: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will reduce your chariots to cinders, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
units.rightText: Behold, I am against thee, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions; and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.

units.leftText: Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey.
units.rightText: Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and rapine; the prey departeth not.

units.leftText: The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, galloping horse and bounding chariot!
units.rightText: The noise of the whip, and the noise of the rattling of wheels, and prancing horses, and bounding chariots,

units.leftText: Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear; heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end— they stumble over their dead—
units.rightText: the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, and the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies; they stumble upon their bodies;—

units.leftText: because of the many harlotries of the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery, who betrays nations by her prostitution and clans by her witchcraft.
units.rightText: because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the well-favored harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.

units.leftText: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
units.rightText: Behold, I am against thee, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will uncover thy skirts upon thy face; and I will show the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.

units.leftText: I will pelt you with filth and treat you with contempt; I will make a spectacle of you.
units.rightText: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazing-stock.

units.leftText: Then all who see you will recoil from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?’ Where can I find comforters for you?”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?

units.leftText: Are you better than Thebes, stationed by the Nile with water around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?
units.rightText: Art thou better than No-amon, that was situate among the rivers, that had the waters round about her; whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?

units.leftText: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.
units.rightText: Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers.
leftNotes: 3:9 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her dignitaries, and all her nobles were bound in chains.
units.rightText: Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity; her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets; and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.

units.leftText: You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy.
units.rightText: Thou also shalt be drunken; thou shalt be hid; thou also shalt seek a stronghold because of the enemy.

units.leftText: All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs; when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater!
units.rightText: All thy fortresses shall be like fig-trees with the first-ripe figs: if they be shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.

units.leftText: Look at your troops — they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.
units.rightText: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women; the gates of thy land are set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire hath devoured thy bars.

units.leftText: Draw your water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses. Work the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln!
units.rightText: Draw thee water for the siege; strengthen thy fortresses; go into the clay, and tread the mortar; make strong the brickkiln.

units.leftText: There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you down and consume you like a young locust. Make yourself many like the young locust; make yourself many like the swarming locust!
units.rightText: There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off; it shall devour thee like the canker-worm: make thyself many as the canker-worm; make thyself many as the locust.

units.leftText: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The young locust strips the land and flies away.
units.rightText: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the canker-worm ravageth, and fleeth away.

units.leftText: Your guards are like the swarming locust, and your scribes like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where.
units.rightText: Thy princes are as the locusts, and thy marshals as the swarms of grasshoppers, which encamp in the hedges in the cold day, but when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.

units.leftText: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your officers sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them.
units.rightText: Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; thy nobles are at rest; thy people are scattered upon the mountains, and there is none to gather them.

units.leftText: There is no healing for your injury; your wound is severe. All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall, for who has not experienced your constant cruelty?
units.rightText: There is no assuaging of thy hurt; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the report of thee clap their hands over thee; for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
